title: Telemetry Log Record
description: Structured JSON log-record standard for every SupremeAI service (#38). One record = one line of newline-delimited JSON (JSONL). The seven top-level fields are frozen: additionalProperties:false — anything service-specific belongs inside context, never beside it. Level vocabulary is lowercase; Python emitters map DEBUG→debug, WARNING→warn, CRITICAL→fatal. trace_id standardizes the correlation id the control plane already threads per action (AuditLogger.correlationId, infrastructure/mcp-control-plane/src/audit/audit.ts). agent_id reuses the exact api-schemas/heartbeat.schema.json pattern; non-agent infrastructure emits the empty string (the same empty-when-N/A convention heartbeat.task_id already uses). Metric emission paired with this standard is declared in $defs/MetricConventions — the OpenTelemetry metric registry (three families: request duration, tokens consumed, agent task completion) whose concrete entries ride as examples. Reference parser: examples/telemetry-logger/logger.py (zero-dependency, mirrors the examples/gateway_client.py house style).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC emission time (e.g. 2026-10-16T10:18:15Z). Identical convention to heartbeat.schema.json timestamp and the new Date().toISOString() already shipped in audit.ts.

level.description: Severity of the record. fatal = the process cannot continue (fail-honest terminal state); error = the operation failed but the process continues; warn = degraded-but-operational (e.g. a visibility-scoped dependency quietly skipped); info = normal operational milestone; debug = development detail that production emitters MUST drop by default.

trace_id.description: Correlation identifier propagated across every service one logical operation touches; all records of that operation share exactly one trace_id. Accepts UUIDs, W3C 32-hex trace ids, and prefixed ids (minimum length 8). This is the existing correlationId concept from audit.ts, given one standard name across the federation.

agent_id.description: Identifier of the agent whose lifecycle produced the record — byte-identical pattern to api-schemas/heartbeat.schema.json agent_id. Empty string when the emitter is non-agent infrastructure (gateway, control plane, studio) — the same empty-when-N/A convention heartbeat.schema.json task_id uses.

component.description: Emitting service/process, lowercase. Known values today: gateway, mcp-tower, orchestrator, memory, agent, command, skills, browser, studio, sdk, infrastructure (ECOSYSTEM_MAP.md §2). Deliberately an open pattern rather than an enum: new services join without a schema bump, while the x-metric-conventions cardinality rule still bounds attribute values.

message.description: Human-readable summary. One-record-one-line semantics: emitters MUST NOT embed raw newlines; payloads belong in context, never concatenated into message.

context.description: Structured key/value payload. Values MUST be JSON scalars, arrays, or objects nested at most 4 levels deep. Reserved conventional keys (aligning with shipped surfaces): provider, action, status, error — the AuditLogEntry fields already shipped in audit.ts; latency_ms — carried on the terminal record of a request chain, the measurement source for supremeai.request.duration; model and usage{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens} — field names identical to the gateway.openapi.yaml chat-completion usage block; event — 'task.completed' | 'task.failed' for agent task terminal outcomes. HARD PROHIBITIONS: no credentials, api keys, provider keys, prompts, payloads, tenant ids, or personal data — context carries shape, never content (SECRETS_MODEL.md / Zero-Admin posture).

MetricConventions.description: Contract shape for ONE OpenTelemetry metric declaration paired with this log standard (#38). The registry's concrete entries ride in examples below. Emission is OPTIONAL per service; when a service emits these metrics, name, unit, and required_attributes MUST match exactly — metric identity is a contract, not a suggestion. Naming rule: dot-separated lowercase names starting with 'supremeai.' (domain.entity[.qualifier]); units from the fixed set {ms, tokens, task}; attribute keys snake_case; attribute values MUST be low-cardinality enums or fixed identifiers — never tenant ids, api keys, prompts, payloads, or free-form labels (cardinality guard).

name.description: Dot-separated lowercase metric name with the mandatory 'supremeai.' prefix.

unit.description: UCUM-friendly unit from the fixed set this standard declares.

description.description: What the metric measures, including the driving contract it is the measurement plane for.

required_attributes.description: Attribute keys that MUST accompany every data point; values low-cardinality only.

attribute_enums.description: Optional closed value-sets per attribute key (e.g. outcome, token_type).

log_source.description: Where in a telemetry-log record the measurement originates, per the reserved context keys.

examples.name: supremeai.request.duration
examples.description: End-to-end request latency per emitting component. Measurement plane for the task-router budget rule latency_sla_missed→queue_and_retry (api-schemas/task-router.schema.json CostBudgetRules, ordered when→then, first match wins) and for the latencyMs the live health plane already exposes per service.
examples.log_source: context.latency_ms on the terminal record of a request chain (records sharing one trace_id).

examples.name: supremeai.tokens.consumed
examples.description: LLM token consumption, one increment per completion, split by token_type. Measurement plane for the task-router CostBudgetRules ceilings per_task_max_input_tokens / per_task_max_output_tokens and max_cost_per_task_usd.
examples.log_source: context.usage.prompt_tokens and context.usage.completion_tokens — field names identical to the usage block of api-schemas/gateway.openapi.yaml /v1/chat/completions.

examples.name: supremeai.agent.task.completion
examples.description: Agent task terminal outcomes; completion_rate = success ÷ (success + failure) over any fixed window. Lifecycle vocabulary from api-schemas/heartbeat.schema.json (agents hold task_ids; empty agent_id records never count here).
examples.log_source: context.event = 'task.completed' | 'task.failed' on records whose agent_id is non-empty.
